title: On The Simplest Quantum-Secure Block Cipher
authors: Gorjan Alagic, Joseph Carolan, Christian Majenz, Saliha Tokat
abstract: Pseudorandom permutations are ubiquitous in theoretical and applied cryptography. PRPs that offer security even against adversaries making quantum queries are of increasing interest, and used in applications ranging from constructing pseudorandom unitaries to separating SZK from BQP.   A successful framework for constructing classically-secure PRPs is the key-alternating Even-Mansour approach, which interleaves applications of public permutations with additions of round keys. The single-round construction is already classically secure in the ideal permutation model (IPM), with added rounds offering improved concrete security. However, in the quantum-query setting, the status of this framework is presently unclear. A simple quantum-query attack based on Simon's algorithm breaks the one-round cipher. For two or more rounds, security is only known against non-adaptive adversaries who must prepare all queries in advance.   In this work, we show that the two-round Even-Mansour cipher is information theoretically secure in the IPM against adversaries making polynomially-many adaptive forward and inverse quantum queries to all available oracles. Our proof uses compressed permutation oracles and a specially crafted isometry relating the ideal and real experiments. We also show that this construction is minimal, in the sense that essentially any cipher constructed via a single call to a public permutation is quantumly insecure.
summary: This paper establishes the quantum security of a specific two-round block cipher construction (Even-Mansour) within the Ideal Permutation Model. It proves that this cipher acts as a quantum pseudorandom permutation against adaptive quantum adversaries. The work is significant for advancing the theoretical understanding of quantum-secure primitives in cryptography.
main_problem: The paper aims to construct and prove the quantum security of Pseudorandom Permutations (PRPs) using the Key-Alternating Cipher (KAC) framework in the quantum-query setting.
main_result: The two-round Even-Mansour cipher is proven to be information theoretically secure (a qPRP) in the Ideal Permutation Model against polynomially-many adaptive forward and inverse quantum queries.
method: The security proof utilizes a hybrid argument, employing an isometry and bounding the distinguishability advantage between the real and ideal quantum distributions.
model_or_system: The model is the Ideal Permutation Model (IPM) extended to the Q2 setting, involving quantum oracles for permutations ($P_1, P_2$) and the cipher structure $E_{k_1,k_2,k_3}(x)$.
key_observables: The distinguishability advantage of a quantum algorithm distinguishing the real world from the ideal world, and the success probability of the quantum distinguisher.
important_parameters: Query complexity ($q$), domain size ($N$), and the number of rounds (specifically two rounds).
main_assumptions: The proof relies on the use of compressed permutation oracles (CPO) and specific algebraic manipulations of quantum states in the Hadamard basis.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes detail complex algebraic derivations involving bounding differences between quantum operators ($	ext{cORVp}\Gamma^2 -Vp\Gamma^2	ext{cOI}$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general framework for quantum security, proving the two-round security via a hybrid argument, and then detailing the complex algebraic steps required to bound the difference between the ideal and real world quantum operations.
why_interesting: While focused on cryptography, the techniques developed—especially the use of isometries and bounding quantum state differences—are highly relevant to analyzing the security and distinguishability of quantum processes in quantum information theory.
